market_summary: Global equities remain near all-time highs with AI-driven capex spending fueling gains in cloud/semis names (NVDA, MSFT) while consumer-facing tech (TSLA, META, AAPL) shows more divergence. Singapore banks continue to outperform on strong 1H26 earnings, led by OCBC and DBS, while STI has stabilized near 5,675 after a brief pullback, supported by easing oil prices. Rate-sensitive and REIT-like plays (S68.SI, C38U.SI) and telecom (Singtel) are lagging, showing negative 1-3m momentum despite corporate actions like Singtel's data-centre IPO plan. Volatility remains elevated in high-beta AI/EV names (TSLA, META, NVDA), creating both momentum and mean-reversion opportunities.

picks.thesis: OCBC has the strongest earnings momentum among SG banks, beating expectations in 1H26 driven by wealth fee income, and is compounding a powerful uptrend (+97% 1y, +3.6% 1m) while sitting just 0.8% off its 52w high with a very shallow 6.1% max drawdown - a sign of persistent institutional buying.
picks.news: DBS and OCBC outperformed expectations in 2QFY2026 results (2026-08-14); OCBC net profit +5% YoY in 1Q26 (2026-06-22).
picks.risks: A sharp rate cut cycle or credit quality shock in SG banks could reverse the wealth-income tailwind; a broad market pullback would hit high-beta financials hardest.

picks.thesis: DBS also beat expectations in 1H26 with record profit, is up 55% over 1 year and trading only 0.8% below its 52w high, showing steady uptrend continuation (vs MA200 +22.4%) alongside sector-wide strength in SG financials.
picks.news: DBS and OCBC outperformed expectations, DBS posted record 1Q26 profit of S$2.93bn (2026-06-22, 2026-08-14).
picks.risks: Valuation is stretched after a 36% 6-month rally; any miss on NIM guidance or regional credit stress could trigger profit-taking.

picks.thesis: Microsoft is one of the clear winners of AI monetization divergence, with cloud/Azure growth impressing Wall Street; strong recent momentum (+3.7% day, +38.4% 3m, +8.5% vs MA50) reflects durable re-rating around AI infrastructure demand.
picks.news: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon impressed with strong cloud/AI growth while Meta, Apple and Tesla faced pressure (2026-08-06); nearly $2T in cap shifts after Q2 earnings (2026-07-31).
picks.risks: Currently 4.8% below 52w high and volatility is high (32.5% annualized); a slowdown in enterprise AI spend or capex guidance miss would hurt the thesis.

picks.thesis: Nvidia's data center revenue is accelerating almost entirely on AI GPU demand (+92% YoY), and major hyperscaler clients continue to ramp capex; the stock is still 4.5% below its 52w high, leaving room to run versus the AI capex supercycle narrative.
picks.news: NVIDIA posted record quarterly revenue of $81.6B with data center at $75.2B (+92% YoY) driven by AI infrastructure spend (2026-07-31).
picks.risks: Any signs of hyperscaler capex digestion/slowdown, export restrictions, or a broader AI-bubble unwind (high 37.8% volatility) could sharply reverse gains.

picks.thesis: Tesla is guiding capex above $25B for 2026 to fund AI/robotics ambitions, pressuring margins and cash flow, and the stock has already logged its worst week in over a month; with -15.5% 1y return, -24% from 52w high, and elevated 46% volatility, sentiment remains fragile versus peers who are monetizing AI more directly.
picks.news: Tesla capex to exceed $25B in 2026 amid AI ramp; stock down over 6% in a week (2026-08-25); Tesla/Musk singled out as lagging AI monetization winners (2026-08-06).
picks.risks: A strong FSD/robotaxi update, surprise margin beat, or short squeeze on high-beta momentum could invalidate the short quickly given Tesla's history of violent rallies.

picks.thesis: Singapore Exchange has weakened noticeably, down 11.4% in the last month and 7.5% below its 50-day moving average despite a still-positive 1-year return, suggesting momentum has turned negative even as the broader STI stabilizes - a divergence that often precedes further underperformance.
picks.news: Broader Singapore market stabilizing near 5,675 after a pullback, with SGX lagging that recovery (2026-09-22).
picks.risks: Higher trading volumes from volatility spikes or new listing/IPO activity (e.g., any large SGX-hosted IPO) could quickly reverse the negative momentum.

picks.thesis: Singtel shows persistent negative momentum (-14.2% 6m, -5.1% 1m, -7.2% vs MA200) despite the positive-sounding India data centre IPO news, implying the market has not yet rewarded the announcement and core telecom fundamentals remain under pressure.
picks.news: Singtel weighing potential IPO for India data centre business under Nxera (2026-09-21).
picks.risks: If the IPO process advances with strong terms/valuation, sentiment could turn quickly positive and squeeze the short; dividend support also limits downside.
